about: Tempo-grid analysis of dinle_2 (full mix + isolated vocal). All times in seconds. Unless stated otherwise, times are on the timeline of dinle_2_vokal.wav.

inputs.mix: dinle_2.mp3 (decoded with ffmpeg to 44.1 kHz mono)

summary.bpm_note: on the timeline of dinle_2_vokal.wav (the file the lines are cut from); 116.006 on the decoded dinle_2.mp3; use 116.0 for the new backing
summary.meter: 4/4 at 116 (drum loop is a 1-beat boom-chick; harmonic unit 4 beats)
summary.statement: All 28 lines start ON the downbeat, none is a pickup. The first sound of a line (including consonants like "Ç", "K") begins on average 18 ms before the downbeat (range -41..+14 ms, SD 14 ms = 0.03 beat); the first vowel is reached on average 9 ms after it (median +3 ms, range -19..+55 ms). Line 2 ("Çiftliğinde") has the largest spread between the two: consonant 34 ms early, vowel 37 ms late. A half-beat pickup would be -259 ms.
summary.placement_recipe: To keep the same feel on a new 116 BPM backing: for each line (or the L3+L4 chunk) put the sample at time `downbeat` of dinle_2_vokal.wav exactly on the new bar line, i.e. new_time = new_bar_start + (t - downbeat). Start the cut at least 60 ms before the downbeat (earliest sound is 41 ms early); `quietest_point_before_line` gives a clean cut point before L1, L2 and L3 (dip of -41 dB or deeper); L3->L4 is legato (dip only -11..-27 dB) and should stay one chunk.
summary.confidence: beat grid/tempo and "on the beat, no pickup": high. Bar-level choice (line start = beat 1, not beat 3): medium-high. Nothing was checked by ear.

method_A_fullband_spectral_flux.description: onset envelope = half-wave rectified log-magnitude spectral flux 30 Hz-16 kHz (hop 5.8 ms); tempo/phase = (BPM, phase) maximising the mean envelope on the beat grid; autocorrelation as a second read-out

method_B_kick_lowfreq_40_120Hz.description: kick/bass band 40-120 Hz amplitude envelope, log-rise half-wave rectified; same grid search and autocorrelation

third_opinion_librosa_beat_track.note: librosa quantises to its 5.8 ms hop (89 frames = 0.51664 s = 116.13 BPM); like method A it locks to the OFF-beat eighth (phase about 0.274 s = half a beat + ~15 ms)

per_window_summary.note: window search step 0.02 BPM; a 20 s window resolves about +-0.03 BPM

fine_drift_check.description: 10 s windows every 5 s: position (ms) of the steepest rise of full-rate band envelopes folded over an exact 116.000 BPM beat; a straight line = constant tempo slightly different from 116.000

refined_lattice_mix_timeline.definition: beat time = steepest rise of the high-frequency transient of the on-beat hit (hats 8-16 kHz) / of the off-beat "chick" minus half a beat; the kick low-frequency body (120-300 Hz) rises about 6 ms later

vocal_only.note: onsets of the 28 lines (vocal-stem timeline) regressed on the lattice beat numbers; uses the mix only for the integer beat numbers

result.statement: Tempo is constant (machine grid). Mix: 116.006 BPM; the isolated-vocal file runs 78 ppm faster than the decoded mix, so on the vocal file the same grid is 116.015 BPM. Both round to 116.0; the difference from exactly 116.000 is 5 ms (mix) / 13 ms (vocal file) over 100 s and less than 1 ms inside one 2-bar chunk.

methods_compared.statement: The two methods agree on the eighth-note lattice within about 6 ms but choose different halves: full-band flux (A) and librosa lock to the off-beat eighth, the kick band (B) to the on-beat eighth.

half_beat_question.observation: Drum/accompaniment pattern is "boom-chick": kick + bass note + hat on one eighth, chord strum/"chick" (300 Hz-8 kHz) + hat on the other eighth.
reasons: kick drum sounds on every one of these eighths (four on the floor) and the bass notes change there (root/fifth)
the file itself starts on that eighth (first transient at t = 0.00 s) and the intro accents fall on it
all 28 sung lines begin within -41..+14 ms of such an eighth; with the opposite choice every line and almost every stressed syllable would be syncopated by exactly half a beat
full-band onset methods prefer the other eighth only because the mid/high "chick" has more spectral flux than the kick

beat_phase.per_verse_note: Deviation (ms) of three local estimates from the global lattice in a 20-beat window around each verse. Hats and kick stay within +-7 ms and show no trend, so one global lattice is valid at every verse; only the BAR phase changes between verses.

timeline_alignment_mix_vs_vocal_stem.statement: The isolated vocal is not sample-locked to the decoded mp3: waveform correlation is weak (phase not preserved), and its events drift from about 4 ms later than the mix at the start to about 4 ms earlier at the end (78 ppm). Measured with two envelope/spectrogram correlations per sung line; a straight line fits within about 1.5 ms. Downbeats are converted with this line.

downbeat.bars_are: 4 beats (2.069 s); the original has an irregular number of beats between verses, so the bar phase is anchored per verse

hypotheses.statement: each sung line starts ON the downbeat of its bar (line onset beat = beat 1)
bar lines lie two beats later: each line starts on beat 3 of the previous bar (half-bar pickup)
hypotheses.verdict: not supported; cannot be excluded by drum accents alone (the drum loop repeats every beat)

hypotheses.statement: bar lines one beat earlier or later (line starts on beat 2 or 4)
hypotheses.verdict: rejected: bass root (A) is on the line-onset beat and two beats later, the fifth (E) on the beats between, in all 7 verses

hypotheses.statement: the beat is the "chick" eighth and lines are half-beat pickups

E1_intro.text: The file starts with a 4-beat guitar/banjo pattern that repeats from t=0: strongest on-beat attacks on beats 0, 4, 8, a chord colour change (G) on beats 3 and 7, drums enter with a 2-beat fill on beats 10-11, and verse 1 starts on beat 12 = 3 bars after the start.

E2_bass_pattern.text: Bass per beat, counted from each verse onset: position 0 = A (root), 1 = E (fifth), 2 = A, 3 = E or a turnaround note (B or C leading back to A). The turnaround note occurs only on position 3, i.e. on the last beat before a line-onset-type beat.

E3_harmony.text: Accompaniment chroma by position: tonic colour strongest on position 0, dominant (E major triad) strongest on position 3, extra colour tones (F, C) on position 2. The only real chord change inside a verse (to the dominant) happens at the start of line 4 (position 12 = a line onset).

E4_same_alignment_in_all_verses.text: The 16-beat chroma sequence under the vocal of verses 2-7 matches verse 1 best at shift 0 beats (not at +-2 or +-4): the accompaniment is locked to the sung lines identically in every verse.

E5_structure_between_verses.text: After line 4 the band continues in 4-beat groups that start exactly where line 4 ends (bass A E A E | A E A B ...). In every gap the turnaround note (bass B or C) falls on beat 23 or 27 counted from the verse onset, i.e. on the 4th beat of such a group. In 3 of the 6 verse-to-verse transitions (1->2, 2->3, 6->7, and again before the tag after verse 7) the next verse starts on the very next beat. The other three are where the irregular beat counts come from: an inserted 2-beat break before verse 4 (everything stops on the off-beat at 46.30 s), one extra beat before verse 5, and one more full 4-beat bar before verse 6. So the irregular bars are in the instrumental gaps, not inside the sung verses, and each verse restarts the 4-beat pattern on its first sung beat.

E6_periodicity.text: Beat-feature self-similarity is higher at lag 4 than at lag 2 and at lag 8 than at lag 6: a 4-beat unit exists.

E7_weak_or_neutral.text: Drum accents do not separate H0 from H2: kick and hats repeat every beat. Small 4-beat cues: off-beat low-frequency hit after position 1, slightly more cymbal energy on position 0, slightly more low-band pickup after position 3.

E8_lyrics.text: Judgement, not measurement: every line is a closed unit that starts with a syllable exactly on a beat and ends on/after the 4th beat (L1: syllables on 0, 0.5, 1.5, 1.9, 3.0; L4: 0, 1, 2, 3). With H0 that is "one line = one bar", which is also how Old MacDonald is phrased; with H2 every line would straddle a bar line.

confidence.that_strong_beat_is_beat_1_rather_than_b: medium-high (harmonic and structural evidence, all pointing the same way; no drum-accent proof; not checked by ear)

downbeat.practical_consequence: For re-placing the lines it does not matter whether H0 or H2 is true: the line onset sits on a root-bass beat in both, and the new form puts each line at the start of a bar. Use the downbeat times given per line.

onset_definitions.onset: acoustic start of the first syllable in the isolated vocal: first spectral-flux peak (512-sample window, 0.73 ms hop, 90 Hz-8 kHz) after the energy dip that precedes the word; includes initial consonants. Agrees with a plain -20 dB envelope threshold within 6 ms (mean +3 ms) on the 19 lines preceded by silence.
onset_definitions.vowel_onset: first time after `onset` at which the voiced band (90-1200 Hz, 5 ms RMS) is within 6 dB of the first-syllable peak; a proxy for the perceived attack
onset_definitions.downbeat: time of the bar line the line belongs to (hypothesis H0), on the vocal-file timeline; downbeat_mix_timeline is the same instant on the decoded mp3
onset_definitions.offset: offset_sec = onset - downbeat; offset_beats = offset_sec / beat period; negative = before the downbeat
onset_definitions.accuracy: onset about +-5 ms for vowel-initial lines, +-10 ms for consonant-initial and legato (L4) lines; downbeat about +-3 ms relative to the drum transients plus +-2 ms timeline conversion

side_observation_for_the_arranger.note: Not part of this task, reported because it was measured: the ORIGINAL accompaniment is centred on A, not C. Bass alternates A (root) / E (fifth) every beat, chords are A(m) and E; under line 4 the bass goes E E A. The reciting tone E4 is therefore the fifth of A in the original, and the final C4 its minor third. This does not change the timing results.

extra_repeats_not_used.note: the two extra "Dinle bak, dinle bak" after verse 7 start on lattice beats 195 and 207 (about 100.86 s and 107.07 s on the mix timeline); not analysed further

not_verified: No listening was possible. Everything above is measurement. In particular the bar-level decision (H0 vs H2) and the claim that the placement "feels" the same are not verified by ear.
reproduce: run kod/run_all.sh (scripts 00..15); detailed intermediate results are in the other *.json files of this folder
